scimapR 0.4.0.9000

    Changelog

    Source: NEWS.md

    scimapR (development version)

    • New synthetic example files shaped like a Web of Science export of three invented military-medical units and their civilian partners: example_realuse_corpus.rds (150 works), example_realuse_reference.csv (a publication-tracker reference list) and example_realuse_affiliation_dict.csv (an affiliation dictionary). See the “Real-use fixture” section of ?sm_example_files.

    • The examples of sm_audit_funding() and sm_audit_summary() run offline: they no longer send one Crossref request per DOI of the example corpus when R CMD check --as-cran runs \donttest{} code. The live lookup is shown in an example that runs only in interactive sessions.

    • sm_audit_summary() no longer sends web requests by default. Its new online argument controls the funding audit, which looks up every DOI on Crossref: with the default online = FALSE that audit is reported as not run unless a precomputed sm_audit_funding() result is passed, and online = TRUE runs it as before.

    • sm_certificate(), sm_cite_corpus() and citation-maturity cut-offs (sm_citation_maturity(), sm_its(outcome = "cnci")) accept numeric, character, Date and POSIXct timestamps in metadata$build_date and metadata$last_refresh. Numbers are read as seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, as corpora restored from tables store them, and implausible numbers (such as milliseconds) are ignored with a message. Text is read as ISO 8601 (a date, or a date and time with an optional Z or +hh, +hhmm or +hh:mm offset); other text counts as missing. Certificates write their timestamps in UTC, for example 2026-10-17T11:45:00Z, still read the older form, and print the creation time in UTC.

    • sm_metric_fnci() gains min_cell and by_type (opt-in fallback baselines) and informs when many works sit in tiny cells; sm_its(outcome = "cnci") and sm_metric_summary(metric = "cnci") show that message too. With min_cell, a work whose field-year cell is too small falls back to its field in the neighbouring years and then to its year, field may list several ;-separated categories, and the result reports n_cell and baseline. by_type = TRUE gives articles and reviews baselines of their own.

    • sm_metric_fnci(classification = "manual") reports a factor field by its labels instead of its integer codes.

    • sm_metric_fnci(classification = "mesh") never uses a MeSH check tag (such as Humans, Female or Adult) or a descriptor of study design or statistics (such as Retrospective Studies, Risk Factors or Treatment Outcome) as a work’s field. sm_fetch_pubmed(), sm_read_pubmed_xml() and sm_enrich_concepts(source = "mesh") now record each MeSH heading’s major-topic flag as its concept score (1 for a major topic, 0 otherwise; before, always NA), so the field is a major topic of the work. Headings without scores, as from other sources, give the work’s heading that is most frequent in the corpus instead of the first one listed, with a message.

    • sm_cluster_evolution(link_by = "cluster_id") follows a global clustering across windows; snapshots gain share. Each cluster present in two consecutive windows gives one transition, except the noise cluster named by the new noise argument (default 0L).

    • sm_affiliation_match() matches dictionary patterns in Unicode mode, so \w and \b work on non-ASCII names; new sm_affiliation_unmatched() lists unmatched affiliation strings. Unicode mode is the new default, for the postcode signal too: \w, \b, \d, \s and POSIX classes such as [[:alpha:]] now treat umlauts, accented letters and other non-ASCII letters, digits and spaces like ASCII ones. A pattern can stop matching if it used \W, \S, \D or \B to stand for a non-ASCII letter, or if it relied on \b between an ASCII and a non-ASCII letter: the shipped pattern \bnato\b no longer matches “NATO” directly followed by an umlaut. The new argument unicode = FALSE restores the earlier ASCII-only matching. sm_attribute_institution() has no such argument and matches in Unicode mode when it runs sm_affiliation_match() itself; the Details of ?sm_affiliation_match show how to get its earlier results.

    • sm_screen_regex() matches its terms as written, case-insensitively and in Unicode mode like sm_affiliation_match(), so a term can stop matching in the same ways (new argument unicode, default TRUE). It no longer lowercases the patterns, which turned \W, \S, \D and \B into \w, \s, \d and \b, and a corpus with a single work now gets one screening row instead of several.

    • sm_its() no longer fails when a year has no finite outcome, sm_did() no longer fits silently on fewer years, and sm_synth() no longer passes such years to tidysynth; these years are dropped with a warning and reported (dropped_years). sm_did() drops them per group, and sm_synth() for every unit so that its panel stays balanced. For outcome = "cnci", works with an infinite impact value are left out of the yearly mean, and a year without usable impact counts as dropped even when it is citation-immature, so dropped_years and provisional_years never share a year.

    • The confidence intervals of sm_its() and sm_did() use the t distribution with the residual degrees of freedom when the model estimates its dispersion, as their p-values already did: the default Gaussian fits of sm_did() and of sm_its() for "share_q1", "cnci" and "leadership", and quasi families. These intervals are wider than before and agree with the p-values. Poisson fits (the sm_its() default for "count") keep normal intervals and now warn when the counts are overdispersed, suggesting family = "quasipoisson".

    • With outcome = "count", sm_its(), sm_did() and sm_synth() count a year without works as 0, over every year from the first to the last publication year of the corpus, instead of leaving the year out; filter the corpus to the analysis window first. sm_synth() aborts when a unit has no works.

    • sm_its() checks the years that remain after all exclusions (years without a usable value and, for "cnci", citation-immature years) instead of before the citation-immature cut. It needs at least 4 years, 2 or more before intervention_year and 2 or more from it on, and aborts otherwise, or when a level or slope change cannot be estimated, instead of silently fitting a model without those terms. On exactly 4 years a Gaussian or quasi-family fit has no residual degrees of freedom, and sm_its() now warns that its standard errors, intervals and p-values are NaN. sm_did() needs 4 years per group, with years before and from intervention_year, and sm_synth() 4 panel years, 2 of them before it.

    • sm_its(), sm_did() and sm_synth() check intervention_year the same way and abort unless it is one whole year, given as a number or as text such as "2020". Before, sm_did() and sm_synth() truncated a year such as 2020.5 and read TRUE as the year 1, and all three read a factor or a date by its internal number.

    • Concept vocabularies are now a controlled set (sm_concept_vocabularies()); sm_to_bibliometrix() DE and keyword co-word networks work for file-based corpora. sm_corpus() and sm_corpus_from_tables() rename legacy and common spellings such as "keywords-author", "keyword" or "MEDLINE" to these names, with a message, and the functions that select concepts by vocabulary read every one of these spellings. Values that name no known vocabulary are kept as written and listed in the same message, so a corpus built from such tables now reports them each time; name a vocabulary of your own "custom". DE holds each work’s author keywords; a work without any falls back to its OpenAlex concepts, so corpora built from OpenAlex keep their DE, and arXiv and bioRxiv categories stay out of it as before. sm_network_coword() gains vocabulary: field = "keywords" uses the author keywords by default and, in a corpus without any, the indexer keywords (such as Keywords Plus or MeSH) with a message; a corpus with neither gives an empty network, now with a message. With field = "concepts", vocabulary keeps only the vocabularies named.

    • sm_read_wos() reads the Web of Science categories (WC) into the new vocabulary wos-category; wos-subject-category keeps the research areas (SC). Corpora read from Web of Science files therefore have more concept rows, which changes the results of functions that use every concept whatever its vocabulary: sm_network_coword(field = "concepts"), sm_plot_thematic_map(), sm_author_trajectory() and the corpus hash (sm_hash_corpus()). sm_author_trajectory() now counts a concept name once per work in its dominant topics and novelty (before, a name that a work had in two vocabularies counted twice), so a category with the same name as a research area of the work leaves the trajectory unchanged.

    • sm_to_bibliometrix() exports C1, RP, ID, WC, SC, UT, SN/EI, J9/JI, EM, AF, one AU entry per author, CR in Web of Science form and DB = "ISI" for corpora from Web of Science, so bibliometrix::histNetwork() and bibliometrix::rpys() run; C1 round-trips through as_sm_corpus(). Every tag column is present, NA where the corpus has no data. New arguments: keep_extra = FALSE drops the columns without a field tag, and db sets DB. sm_read_wos() now reads the ISSNs and journal abbreviations (SN, EI, J9, JI) into sources (issn_l, issn and the new columns abbreviation and iso_abbreviation), so ISSN lookups now work for corpora read from Web of Science files. It also keeps each author name as the file writes it (such as “Garcia Lopez, M”) in authors$display_name_alternatives, so the export keeps surnames of several words whole, and cited-reference DOIs lose a trailing period. Because of these changes the corpus hash (sm_hash_corpus()) of corpora read from Web of Science files changes too.

    • sm_to_bibliometrix() now upper-cases the text fields that bibliometrix keeps upper-case (as convert2df() does); DI stays as stored. Its default output changes in a few more ways: AU holds names as SURNAME INITIALS (such as VALDEZ P) instead of the stored display names, SR is built as convert2df() builds it (first author, year and journal abbreviation, made unique) and gives the row names, NR counts the items of CR instead of the reference rows, DE separates its terms with ;, and the tag columns come first. AU_CO is no longer written, so bibliometrix reads the countries from C1 (bibliometrix::metaTagExtraction(M, "AU_CO")) as it does for convert2df() data. With the default keep_extra = TRUE the other columns stay, and the ISO country codes that AU_CO held are in the new column country_code.

    • The "bibliometrix" and "auto" engines of the file readers and as_sm_corpus() for bibliometrix data frames now share one conversion, which also reads the cited references (CR, with the DOI of each reference that has one), the sources (SO, SN, EI, J9, JI), the keywords and categories (DE, ID, WC, SC), the Web of Science accession numbers (UT) and the PubMed IDs; before, these corpora had no references, sources or concepts. Authors keep their full names from AF and get one authorship row per address, linked through the names in C1, and titles and abstracts keep the case of the file. Authors are now told apart by their full names in AF instead of their AU form, so author counts can change; an entry with initials only, or without AF, belongs to the author with the same surname and initials when there is just one. as_sm_corpus() labels the provenance of Web of Science data (DB = "ISI") "wos".

    • sm_coverage_audit(by =) accepts any reference or works column; corpus-side affiliation uses institution matches before country codes. A name is either one of the named dimensions "year", "source" and "affiliation" or a column of the reference data frame (matched case-insensitively) or of works; a dimension found on one side only gets NA for the other side, and a name found on neither side is an error listing the available columns. The affiliation levels of a corpus come from the first of institution_match, institution_name, institution_id and country_code that has a value, with a message naming the column on each side and a warning when a side falls back to country codes. A work counts in every institution of its authors, so per-level counts can add up to more than the total; the overall recall and precision count each record once. In a data-frame reference, "affiliation" now takes an affiliation, affiliations or institution column before a country or country_code column, and "source" a source name before source_id, whatever their order, and the values of each row stay with that row.

    • sm_coverage_audit() and sm_reconcile() identify the rows of a data frame by its UT column (Web of Science accession numbers) or an id, work_id, reference_id or ref_id column only when its values are unique and none is missing; otherwise rows are identified by their position (R000001, …), with a warning. A column named ID next to Web of Science field tags holds the Keywords Plus and is never used. Before, missing or repeated identifiers, such as those of the ID column that sm_to_bibliometrix() writes, made the recall, the breakdowns, n_reference_only and matches$reference_id disagree.

    • sm_coverage_audit() looks up each reference row on its own for recall, so an item that two rows report (one paper reported by two units) counts as found for both instead of only for the first; precision still pairs each corpus record with at most one reference row. n_matched counts the reference rows found and the new element n_corpus_matched the corpus records paired, which print() shows for precision and summary() adds as its last column; the two differ only when reference rows share a corpus record. The new element reference_matches shows for each reference row the corpus record it was found in, as matches does for the corpus records. When a DOI repeats on both sides, its records now pair in order instead of leaving the later ones to the title fallback.

    • The title fallback of sm_coverage_audit() and sm_reconcile() pairs two records only when their publication years differ by at most one (or a year is missing) and never when both have a DOI and the DOIs differ, so serial titles such as annual reports and generic titles such as “Editorial” no longer match across years. A Date or date-time year column of a data frame counts by its calendar year, and a year outside 1000-2999 (such as a day count) as missing.

    • Title matching in sm_coverage_audit() and sm_reconcile(), and the ROR lookup of sm_attribute_institution(), keep the letters and digits of every script when they normalise text. Before, they dropped every non-ASCII letter, so titles in Cyrillic, Greek or other non-Latin scripts never matched and words with umlauts or accents lost letters.

    • sm_count(level = "institution") no longer applies the shipped dictionary sm_affiliation_dict on its own, which credited any “military hospital” or “army hospital” to “Bundeswehr Hospital”. This changes its default counts: each authorship row now takes the first of institution_match, institution_name and institution_id (named by corpus$institutions when listed) that has a value in that row, and otherwise its raw affiliation string, with a warning. Before, one column served every row, so the rows without a value in it were left out, and entity_id was the institution_id whenever any row had one; now it is the label, except for rows labelled through institution_id. After sm_attribute_institution(), which keeps institution_match, the counts therefore follow the dictionary matches instead of their roll-up to ROR ids and names; to count by the vocabulary, replace institution_match by institution_name where that is set (see ?sm_count). Run sm_affiliation_match() with a dictionary of your institutions first to count them.

    • The shipped dictionary sm_affiliation_dict no longer credits a bare “military hospital”, “army hospital” or “armed forces hospital”, which can be a hospital of any country, to “Bundeswehr Hospital”. Its rows for that hospital now need “Bundeswehr”, “German Armed Forces”, “German Army” or “German Military” before “hospital”, or the German name, so sm_affiliation_match() with its default patterns, and sm_attribute_institution() on a corpus that was not matched first, leave other military hospitals unmatched; an English name with “Bundeswehr”, such as “Bundeswehr Hospital”, now matches as well.

    • The WoS reader (both engines), the bibliometrix import and both OpenAlex readers take the corresponding author from the RP field or the OpenAlex is_corresponding flag instead of assuming the first author; the readers of sources without this information record it as unknown (NA). sm_audit_geographic(weight = "corresponding") and the gender audit now find corresponding authors (they used isTRUE() on a column). RP is read in any case, with the older “(reprint author)” and with its names on one line or several, in both engines; namesakes with the same surname and initials are told apart by the address RP gives, and stay unknown when it does not tell them apart. A work whose RP names none of its authors counts as unknown, and so does an OpenAlex work whose authors are all marked false unless its corresponding_author_ids lists one of them. This changes default results: sm_read_lens(), sm_read_ris(), sm_read_scopus(), sm_read_bib(), sm_read_pubmed_xml(), sm_fetch_pubmed(), sm_fetch_crossref() and the other readers and fetchers without corresponding-author data now give NA instead of TRUE for the first author, so sm_to_bibliometrix() exports RP = NA for their corpora, and sm_audit_geographic(weight = "corresponding") reports the countries of the corresponding authors instead of an empty table with coverage 0.

    • Leadership outcomes can be restricted to focal institutions and author roles (institutions, lead_role; institution_aware in sm_did() and sm_synth()); works with an unknown corresponding author, and works without any authorship rows (before counted as not led), leave the default leadership denominator. A work counts as led when an authorship in the role ("corresponding", "first", "last", "first_or_last" or "any_lead") carries one of the institution labels in institution_match, institution_name or institution_id, or the name of that id in corpus$institutions; a label that no authorship carries gives a warning naming the nearest labels. The denominator change applies to sm_its(), sm_did() and sm_synth() alike and changes their default "leadership" results for corpora with unknown corresponding authors, which now include most corpora from readers other than the WoS and OpenAlex readers: a year without a known corresponding author is dropped with a warning, and when no work has one the functions abort and suggest lead_role = "first" or "last" with focal institutions. The print methods state the definition used, which the results keep in leadership.

    • sm_read_wos() links the addresses of C1 to the authors by their whole names, as the bibliometrix engine does: the full name of AF, else the surname and initials, else the surname and first initial. It now writes one authorship row per author and address. Before, it gave each author the first C1 line whose bracket contained the author’s surname anywhere, so a short surname such as “He” or “Li” took the address of “Chen” or “Lin”, an author with several addresses kept only the first, and lines without names linked nobody. In both engines and in as_sm_corpus(), an address that C1 lists without names, as older records do, now belongs to every author of the record, and the bibliometrix engine keeps such a line apart from the address before it. Authorship rows, address-based counts and the corpus hash of corpora read from Web of Science files change.

    • sm_fetch_biorxiv() takes the corresponding author from the author_corresponding field of the bioRxiv API, and sm_read_dimensions() from a Corresponding Authors column, matching the names to the authors by surname and given names or initials; a name that fits two authors equally leaves both unknown. sm_fetch_orcid() records the ORCID holder’s position and corresponding-author flag as unknown (NA); before, the holder was first and corresponding author of every work, which counted as first authorship in the geographic and gender audits.

    • sm_did() reports the works that belong to both the treated and the control group, such as works co-authored by both, which pull the two series together and the estimate toward 0: with a warning when the new argument shared is not set, and in the new element shared_works. shared = "exclude" leaves them out of both series and "lead" gives each to the group of its lead author (lead_role); the default "keep" keeps them in both, as before. sm_did() aborts when treated and control share a label. sm_did() and sm_synth() gain lag and, for outcome = "cnci", now leave out the citation-immature years as sm_its() does and list them in provisional_years, which changes their default "cnci" results.

    • sm_attribute_institution() keeps the institution_id and institution_name of the authorships it does not match, such as the OpenAlex institution ids of a fetched corpus. Before, it set them to NA, so institution counts, the institution h-index and the regional audit lost every institution outside the vocabulary.

    • sm_summary_authors(), sm_summary_period() and the position breakdown of sm_audit_gender() count each author once per work, however many address rows the author has in it, as sm_metric_collab_index() does. Before, an author with two address rows counted twice, so a single-author work did not count as single-authored and the authors per work disagreed with sm_metric_collab_index().

    • OpenAlex fetches and sm_read_openalex_json() keep FWCI, citation percentiles and yearly citation counts (new corpus element citations_by_year); new sm_enrich_openalex_impact() adds them to any corpus by identifier and stops cleanly on HTTP 429; new sm_citation_window(). The works gain the columns fwci, citation_percentile, is_top_10pct, is_top_1pct and citations_as_of (the date of these values); the openalexR engine has no percentile. sm_fetch_openalex() now stops with the same message on HTTP 429, naming the reset time, the remaining budget and the OPENALEX_API_KEY setting, instead of a generic error (native engine) or an empty corpus (openalexR engine), and its openalexR engine now uses OPENALEX_API_KEY too and needs openalexR 3.1.1 or later. sm_enrich_openalex_impact() sends identifiers only, joins nothing when a request fails, and records its step in provenance with the source "openalex_impact" and the kind "enrichment", which sm_rebuild_from_cert() never replays; certificates record the kind of each step. sm_corpus(), sm_corpus_from_tables(), subsetting, sm_bind_corpora(), sm_dedupe(), sm_export_csv(), sm_validate() and sm_hash_corpus() carry citations_by_year; corpora without it keep their hash.

    • sm_metric_summary(metric = "cnci") resolves impact like sm_its() and reports its source as an attribute; both now use works$fwci when works$cnci is absent (ahead of other impact columns and corpus$metrics), which changes sm_its(), sm_did() and sm_synth() results with outcome = "cnci" for such corpora. The attribute impact_source is NA on the n = 0 row, which a corpus without usable impact data still gives; a message names the source for "cnci" and the new metric = "fwci", and the results of sm_its(), sm_did() and sm_synth() keep it as impact_source and print it. sm_its(), sm_did(), sm_synth() and sm_metric_summary() gain min_cell, passed to sm_metric_fnci() when they derive impact from citation counts (default NULL, as before). The error for a corpus without impact data has the class scimapR_no_impact_data.

    • sm_fetch_openalex() and sm_read_openalex_json() fill authorships$raw_affiliation from OpenAlex’s raw_affiliation_strings (joined with "; "), else from affiliations[].raw_affiliation_string, else from the institution names. Before, sm_fetch_openalex() read a field OpenAlex no longer has, so raw_affiliation was NA for every fetched authorship and sm_affiliation_match() matched nothing, and sm_read_openalex_json() kept only the name of the first institution, without the department and unit text that dictionaries match.

    • sm_read_openalex_json() links works to their source (works$source_id). Before, it was NA for every work, so source counts, the source plots and h-index, ISSN lookups in sm_coverage_audit() and SO in sm_to_bibliometrix() came out empty. Sources with the same name but different OpenAlex ids now stay apart.

    • sm_read_openalex_json() reads a saved API response (an object whose results hold the works, compact or pretty-printed), a single work object and newline-delimited files whose lines are responses; before, a saved response gave one empty work or a parse error. It also reads abstracts from abstract_inverted_index when a record has no plain abstract; before, such a record stopped the reader with an error.

    • sm_fetch_openalex() stores ORCIDs without the https://orcid.org/ prefix, as the other readers do, and sm_author_trajectory(orcid =) accepts an ORCID in either form, so sm_researcher_profile() finds its researcher; before, it aborted with “No author found with ORCID” for every researcher with 5 or more works. sm_researcher_profile() gains n_max (default 200, as before).

    • Timestamps given as ISO 8601 text with more than three decimals of a second, such as 2026-10-01T04:12:33.123456 (the form of OpenAlex’s updated_date), are read, for example in metadata$last_refresh; before, they counted as missing.

    • sm_embed_works() with the default model specter2 loads the SPECTER2 adapter through the Python adapters package as the model card describes; it previously failed in SentenceTransformer(). This model needs the Python packages torch, transformers and adapters (install_deps = TRUE installs torch and adapters), the other models need sentence-transformers as before, and the error for a missing package names it. A model that does not load now stops with an error that names the model and gives the Python error.

    • sm_embed_works() gains multilingual models (multilingual-mpnet, multilingual-e5), informs when an English-only model meets a multilingual corpus, warns about works without text, and records the model in the corpus metadata and certificate. Texts for multilingual-e5 start with "query: ", the prefix its model card gives for clustering. The message appears when more than 10% of the works with a known language are not in English; it reads language names such as "German", ISO 639-1 codes such as "de" and ISO 639-2 codes such as "ger". corpus$metadata$embedding records the model, its Hugging Face id and snapshot revision, the text and prefix used, the versions of the Python packages and the time (see ?sm_corpus). sm_certificate() reports them in embedding_info, whose method now names the package or service that made the embeddings, or is "unknown" for embeddings without such a record (before: "recorded").

    • sm_embed_works() leaves works without text out of the embeddings, with a warning giving their number: with the default text = "title_abstract" the works with neither a title nor an abstract, with "title" or "abstract" the works without that field (blank text counts as none). Before, they were all embedded as the same empty text, so they became each other’s nearest neighbours, formed a cluster of their own and stopped sm_plot_landscape(reducer = "tsne"). The row names of corpus$embeddings are the embedded works, and the clustering functions give the other works no cluster (NA), as they do for works missing from a cache loaded with sm_embed_load().

    • sm_embed_works() works on a corpus with a single work; before, it failed with “length of ‘dimnames’ [1] not equal to array extent”.

    • sm_enrich_specter() fetches the SPECTER v2 vectors of Semantic Scholar instead of the API’s default SPECTER v1 and records them in metadata$embedding. It fills gaps only in embeddings from the same source: for embeddings of another model, or of a model that is not recorded, it stops unless you set replace = TRUE (replace them by SPECTER v2 vectors for every work with a DOI) or mix_models = TRUE (keep them and add SPECTER v2 vectors for the other works, recorded as a mix). Before, it silently mixed the vectors of two models when their widths matched, and discarded every existing embedding, with only a warning, when they did not. It now warns about failed requests also with verbose = FALSE, tries a request once more after a short wait when Semantic Scholar answers HTTP 429, and records its provenance rows as an enrichment, which sm_rebuild_from_cert() does not replay.

    • sm_bind_corpora() and sm_build_corpus() gain mix_models. They stop when the embeddings of two corpora record different models in metadata$embedding, or when only one of them records its model, unless mix_models = TRUE, which binds them and records a mix; embeddings of corpora that record no model bind as before. sm_embed_save() keeps the record with the cache and sm_embed_load() restores it, or leaves the model unrecorded for a cache without one, and sm_fetch_semantic_scholar(include_embeddings = TRUE) records its SPECTER v1 vectors.

    • Certificates record local input files with SHA-256 (sm_register_input(), sm_corpus_from_tables(inputs =)); sm_verify_certificate() checks them (base_dir), reports a status per check and warns about inputs it could not find; sm_rebuild_from_cert() names the local inputs it cannot replay. The checks of a verification gain the columns status ("pass", "fail" or "not checked") and location, and the result gains n_not_checked: a check that was not made has pass = NA, and the overall result passes unless a check failed. A relative input path is looked for in base_dir, in the folder of the certificate file, in the working directory and last at the absolute path recorded at registration. Printing a verification now shows a symbol for each check, and printing a certificate the number of local inputs. sm_bind_corpora() keeps the local inputs of both corpora.

    • sm_rebuild_from_cert() replays only the searches of OpenAlex, PubMed and Crossref, through sm_fetch_openalex(), sm_fetch_pubmed() or sm_fetch_crossref() with the engine, filter and n_max they were made with. Before, it cut every search at 1,000 works and sent the file paths of file reads and the placeholder queries of enrichments to the APIs as search text. sm_fetch_openalex(), sm_fetch_pubmed(), sm_fetch_crossref() and sm_corpus_for_question() now record kind, filter and n_max in provenance, and sm_corpus_for_question() records the client package that ran each search ("openalexR", "rentrez" or "rcrossref") as its engine instead of "native", and for Crossref an n_max of at most 1,000, the most its single request returns; the file readers record the kind "file" and the file relative to the working directory, or its name, instead of the path as given; the enrichers record the kind "enrichment"; and certificates write file steps without absolute paths. A message names the steps and local inputs that were not replayed. When a certificate has no search to replay but records file reads or local inputs, the rebuild stops with an error that names them instead of returning an empty corpus; a certificate of only synthetic records, enrichments, refreshes or searches of other sources still gives an empty corpus. A search without a recorded n_max, as in certificates of earlier versions, fetches up to the number of works of the certified corpus. The rebuilt corpus holds the works of the searches and their provenance only.

    • sm_hash_corpus() no longer depends on the order of the columns of a table or of the rows of the embeddings (hash version 2; new argument version), so hashes of new certificates and snapshots differ from earlier ones for the same content. Certificates and snapshots record hash_version, and those written without it are checked with the earlier algorithm (version = 1), so they stay verifiable. The documentation now says that the hash leaves out the provenance table, which records fetch dates, and the metadata, the local inputs included.

    • sm_cluster_label() ignores noise, scores terms by the share of a cluster’s works that use them (so one paper cannot name a cluster), supports bigrams and non-English stop words, and gains method = "keywords". The labels of the default method = "tfidf" change: they hold single words and pairs of adjacent words (new argument ngram, default 1:2), or the longer phrase that two overlapping terms form (such as “exertional heat illness” for “exertional heat” and “heat illness”), that occur in at least 3 of the cluster’s works or 5% of them, whichever is more (new argument min_works), count singular and plural as one term, and leave out the stop words of each work’s language in works$language as well as the English ones, from the stopwords package when it is installed; method = "yake" leaves out these stop words too. The works of the noise cluster (new argument noise, default 0L, as sm_cluster_hdbscan() assigns) get the label NA from every method and no longer count for the labels of the other clusters, so sm_plot_thematic_map(by = "cluster_label") leaves them out; a cluster whose works share no term gets NA too, with a message. The new column cluster_label_basis says how each label was made, for example "tfidf (relaxed)" when no term reached min_works and the terms occur in as few as 2 works, while cluster_label still holds only the terms joined with "; ". method = "keywords" labels clusters by their author and indexer keywords (such as Keywords Plus), and a cluster without keywords by the terms of its titles; the new argument stop_terms leaves out terms such as words every cluster shares.

    scimapR 0.4.0

    Stability contracts, an enrichment materializer, and self-citation-corrected metrics, plus a verify-and-harden pass on three v0.3.0 fixes that recurred in heavy use. All new behaviour is opt-in; no breaking changes.

    Accessor stability contract (A1)

    • New ?scimapR-stability topic documents the package’s accessor return-type contract: a documented accessor’s column set changes only via a lifecycle deprecation and a NEWS.md entry. The audited accessors and their stable shapes are listed there.
    • sm_coverage_breakdowns() gains tidy = TRUE (default): a guaranteed long tibble (dimension, level, n_reference, n_matched, recall, n_corpus, precision, f1). tidy = FALSE returns the legacy recall-only shape. (The silent list -> tibble change between 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 motivated this contract.)

    Controlled vocabularies (B1)

    • Exported sm_affiliation_signals(), sm_affiliation_methods(), and sm_match_types() (with describe = TRUE for level + description). The match_signal, match_method, and coverage match_type columns are now factors with these exact levels, so downstream filtering cannot drift.

    Verify-and-harden (re-reported v0.3.0 fixes)

    These were reported again on a real corpus; each now has a regression test reproducing the recurrence.

    • C1 sm_its(outcome = "cnci"): the resolver now also searches documented impact side columns on works (fnci, rcr, ncs, mncs, field_citation_ratio) and a corpus$metrics table, in addition to works$cnci and works$cited_by_count. With no impact anywhere it errors naming every column inspected. (v0.3 only checked works$cnci / cited_by_count, so impact in a side column still produced “0 observations”.)
    • C2 sm_count(level = "institution"): when structured IDs are absent it now clusters raw_affiliation via sm_affiliation_match() (canonical names where matched, raw string otherwise) with a warning, instead of counting raw strings verbatim. Absent raw affiliation -> 0-row tibble + warning.
    • C3 network plot precompute = TRUE confirmed; the max_nodes cap is now opt-in (NULL default) so large renders are unchanged unless a cap is requested. A ~2,000-node graph builds with precompute = TRUE and re-prints without recomputing layout.

    Enrichment materializer (D1)

    • sm_materialise(corpus, sources, .by = NULL, overwrite = FALSE) joins cached enrichment (named list of tibbles / RDS / parquet paths, or a cache dir) into the matching sub-tibbles by key, returning a validated sm_corpus. Missing keys warn (not error); overlapping columns fill NA unless overwrite = TRUE.
    • Added an internal type-safe row-bind helper (.sm_bind_rows) that returns a typed template instead of a logical-column degenerate when all parts are NULL/empty; audited the package’s existing bind_rows() sites (found safe, guarded behind length checks with typed tibbles).

    Self-citation-corrected metrics (E1, E2, F1)

    • sm_self_citation(corpus, level = c("author", "institution")) computes self-citation from the corpus reference network (quota-light reference overlap; no per-citation API calls), returning by_entity, by_work, and a provenance tibble (citing_work_id, cited_work_id, shared_author_id/shared_institution_id) (F1). Empty references -> warning + typed empty result (no spin).
    • sm_metric_h_index(), sm_metric_g_index(), sm_metric_m_index() gain self_corrected = FALSE; with TRUE the index is recomputed after removing self-citations (author/institution levels). The corrected index is always <= the uncorrected one.

    Provenance (F2)

    • sm_affiliation_summary() now includes example_evidence (a representative matched-evidence string per institution x signal) alongside the factorised match_signal, so a reader can see which signal matched and on what evidence.

    Fixtures

    • inst/extdata/example_self_citation_corpus.rds: a small references-bearing synthetic corpus for self-citation examples/tests.

    scimapR 0.3.0

    Real-use refinements from running v0.2.0 on a ~6,853-work corpus: robustness fixes, friendlier API shapes, two new capabilities, and vignettes that ship in the installed binary. The public API is preserved (deprecation paths only).

    Bug fixes

    • A1 sm_its(outcome = "cnci") no longer fails with a cryptic “Too few yearly observations: 0” when impact lives outside cited_by_count. The resolver now searches, in order, works$cnci, a corpus$metrics table, then works$cited_by_count (deriving FNCI); if none is populated it raises an informative error naming the columns it inspected.
    • A2 sm_count(level = "institution") falls back to authorships$raw_affiliation (with a cli warning that results are un-disambiguated) when structured institution IDs are absent, and warns rather than returning a silent empty result when no institution data exists.
    • A3 sm_metric_disruption() and sm_metric_novelty() fast-exit with a warning when the reference network is empty/absent instead of spinning; the disruption index was rewritten with O(1) adjacency lookups (no longer O(n^2)) and now shows a cli progress bar. sm_audit_summary() shows a progress bar across its sub-audits.
    • A4 Network plots (sm_plot_citation_network(), sm_plot_collab()) gain precompute = TRUE (eager layout -> a self-contained plain ggplot that prints cheaply in knitr/callr/workflowr subprocesses) and a max_nodes cap (default 200) for very large graphs.

    Ergonomics

    • B1 sm_coverage_audit()$breakdowns is now a single flat tibble (dimension, level, n_reference, n_matched, recall). The previous nested list remains available under $breakdowns_nested for one release. New accessor sm_coverage_breakdowns() returns/filters the flat tibble.
    • B2 sm_affiliation_match() documents its added columns and gains sm_affiliation_summary() — a tidy works/authorships breakdown by institution and match signal, also surfaced as a cli summary on completion.
    • B3 sm_corpus_from_tables() is promoted in the ingestion vignette as the recommended “bring your own relational data” entry point.

    New capabilities

    • C1 sm_coverage_audit(..., index_table = ) additionally assesses journal indexability (reusing sm_journal_in_index()), adding issn/indexable columns to $matches and an $indexability summary. Output is unchanged when index_table is NULL.
    • C2 sm_affiliation_match() returns match_signal (name_token/email_domain/postcode) and match_evidence (the matched substring/domain/code) for an audit trail, plus an opt-in postcode_signal = TRUE matcher (off by default so existing matches are stable).

    Packaging

    • D1 Vignettes now ship in the installed binary; browse them offline with vignette(package = "scimapR") / browseVignettes("scimapR"), or online at the pkgdown site. New inst/extdata/ fixtures: example_affiliation_postcode.csv.

    scimapR 0.2.0

    A new capability layer for research-coverage, affiliation-attribution, and policy-evaluation analyses, plus four reproducible bug fixes. All existing functionality, the sm_corpus schema, bibliometrix interop, and the Shiny app are preserved.

    New features

    Coverage & completeness auditing

    • sm_coverage_audit() computes recall, precision, and F1 of a corpus against a ground-truth reference (manual tracker, ORCID set, repository export, or another sm_corpus), with per-year/source/affiliation breakdowns and full match provenance. Returns an sm_coverage object with print, summary, and autoplot methods.
    • sm_journal_in_index() verifies source coverage against a user-supplied journal master list by normalised ISSN (print and electronic), fully offline.
    • sm_reconcile() performs a content-based symmetric diff (DOI then fuzzy title) returning an sm_reconciliation (in_both/only_a/only_b + provenance), with print/summary/autoplot. sm_diff_corpora() is now marked superseded in favour of it (and continues to work unchanged).

    Affiliation disambiguation & attribution

    • sm_affiliation_match() tags authorships with institutions using a multilingual / synonym-aware dictionary and an email-domain fallback, handling multiple affiliations per author.
    • sm_attribute_institution() rolls matches up to a controlled vocabulary (ROR-backed via an offline ROR table, or a custom vocabulary).
    • sm_affiliation_dict: a default, documented, user-overridable dictionary.

    Causal / policy evaluation

    • sm_its(): turnkey interrupted time series (level + slope terms, counterfactual, autoplot), with automatic exclusion of citation-immature years for citation-based outcomes.
    • sm_did(): difference-in-differences for treated vs control institution sets.
    • sm_synth(): synthetic-control helper (optional tidysynth, graceful error when absent).

    Correctness: citation maturity & counting

    • sm_citation_maturity() flags citation-immature recent years (citation_mature / cnci_provisional), wired into sm_its().
    • sm_count(): full vs fractional counting at institution / author / source level (output credit and fractionally-weighted impact).

    Robust impact summaries

    • sm_metric_summary(robust = TRUE) reports medians with bootstrap CIs and %PP(top-10%) alongside means (base-R resampling by default; boot optional; reproducible via seed).

    Reproducible reporting glue

    • sm_figure_manifest() scans a figure directory into a captions / alt-text / dimensions manifest (optional magick/png, sidecar caption files, CSV/YAML output).
    • sm_corpus_from_tables(): a documented, validating constructor from a relational set of data frames — the recommended ingestion path for arbitrary tabular sources.

    Bug fixes

    • G1 sm_fetch_openalex(engine = "native"): abstract reconstruction from the OpenAlex inverted index is now type-stable and never aborts a fetch on an empty/NULL/malformed record (and no longer passes an invalid .default to purrr::map_chr()).
    • G2 sm_fetch_openalex(engine = "openalexR"): long DOI (or other ID) lists are auto-batched under the API’s OR-filter limit via the new batch_size argument, then row-bound and de-duplicated.
    • G3 sm_read_bib(engine = "bibliometrix"): a field-sparse @article no longer triggers “undefined columns selected”; the scimapR wrapper catches the failure and falls back to the native parser (clean-room rule preserved).
    • G4 native BibTeX engine performance: the parser was rewritten from per-character substr()/grepl() scanning and per-entry tibble construction to linear character-vector scanning with single-pass column assembly. Parsing ~7,000 entries dropped from ~100 s to ~17 s on R 4.5.2 / Windows.

    New data & fixtures

    • inst/extdata/: example_sparse.bib, example_openalex_inverted.json, example_journal_index.csv, example_ror.csv.

    scimapR 0.1.0

    Initial release

    scimapR is a comprehensive R toolkit for bibliometric and scientometric analysis: the reproducible, equity-aware, question-driven, AI-assisted toolkit for working biomedical researchers. Designed as a complement to the foundational bibliometrix package (Aria & Cuccurullo, 2017) with first-class round-trip interop.

    Distinctive features

    • Live corpus refresh. sm_refresh(), sm_staleness(), sm_lock().
    • Research questions as objects. sm_question(), sm_corpus_for_question(), sm_screen_against_question() with optional LLM grounding.
    • Reproducible-by-construction corpus certificates. sm_certificate(), sm_rebuild_from_cert(), sm_verify_certificate().
    • Author trajectory analysis. sm_author_trajectory() with topic pivots, collaborator turnover, emerging-collaborator detection.
    • Equity and representation audit. sm_audit_geographic(), sm_audit_gender(), sm_audit_funding(), sm_audit_oa() with built-in confidence reporting and limitation caveats.
    • LLM-grounded corpus chat. sm_chat() with retrieval-constrained citations.

    Core modules

    • Corpus class (sm_corpus) with provenance and screening tables
    • Clean-room native parsers for 12 bibliographic formats
    • API fetchers for 8 scholarly data sources
    • 8 enrichment functions
    • Bibliometrix round-trip interop
    • 6 network builders (citation, co-citation, coupling, collaboration, co-word, semantic)
    • Embedding and clustering (HDBSCAN, Leiden, k-means)
    • Modern indicators (h/g/m-index, CD index, RCR, FNCI, Uzzi novelty)
    • Viridis-themed publication-ready visualization
    • Multi-format export (PNG 300/600 dpi, PDF, SVG, TIFF, XLSX, ZIP bundles)
    • Comprehensive 13-tab Shiny application
    • Systematic review bridge (PRISMA, Rayyan, Covidence)
